Content: A farmer wants to be sure that pollinator-friendly plants will be able to grow under an area of solar panels. Which `ultext(two)` of these questions should the farmer ask before deciding whether to add solar panels to a field?

A.Choice: What color are the solar panels?

Key.Rationale: The color of the solar panels would not affect whether pollinator-friendly plants would be able to grow under an area of solar panels.

B.Choice: Where will the solar panels come from?

Key.Rationale: The place the solar panels came from would not affect whether pollinator-friendly plants would be able to grow under an area of solar panels.

C.Choice: What type of energy will the solar panels use to produce electricity?

Key.Rationale: The type of energy the solar panels use to produce electricity would not affect whether pollinator-friendly plants would be able to grow under an area of solar panels.

D.Choice: What height should the solar panels be placed off the ground?

Key.Rationale: The height that the solar panels are placed off the ground would affect whether pollinator-friendly plants would be able to grow under an area of solar panels.

E.Choice: How does the shade from the solar panels affect the soil underneath?

Key.Rationale: The shade from the solar panels would affect the soil underneath and whether pollinator-friendly plants would be able to grow under an area of solar panels.

Content: A farmer is considering using solar panels, but the area experiences a certain natural hazard every few `text(years)`. The farmer requests that the solar panels be installed higher off the ground than normal.
Which natural hazard would be `ultext(most likely)` to have its effects reduced by installing solar panels that are higher off the ground, and why?

A.Choice: an earthquake, because higher solar panels are less likely to fall

Key.Rationale: Lower solar panels would be more likely to survive an earthquake with less damage.

B.Choice: a flood, because higher solar panels are less likely to be underwater

Key.Rationale: Higher solar panels would keep the solar panels out of floodwater and allow water to flow beneath the panels.

C.Choice: a hurricane, because higher solar panels are less likely to be damaged by wind and rain

Key.Rationale: Higher solar panels are more likely to be damaged by wind and rain.

D.Choice: a tornado, because higher solar panels are less likely to be removed from the ground by high winds

Key.Rationale: Lower solar panels would be more likely to survive a tornado since higher solar panels would allow for more motion and more potential damage.

Content: Which statement describes a way in which the nonliving parts of a field are affected by plants or animals in the field?

A.Choice: Roots of plants can reduce the erosion of soil.

Key.Rationale: The plants are living things that affect the nonliving parts of a field.

B.Choice: The farmland can generate renewable electricity.

Key.Rationale: The farmland generating renewable electricity is not an interaction between nonliving and living parts of a field.

C.Choice: Solar panels can help keep the soil cool during the `text(day)`.

Key.Rationale: This is an example of `text(two)` nonliving components interacting in a field.

D.Choice: Plants under solar panels can attract pollinators.

Key.Rationale: This idea does not demonstrate an effect of plants or animals on the nonliving parts of a field.

Content: The drawing shows a weasel, an animal that lives in Wisconsin.
problems/WI24G4S/media/4a.jpg
Which `ultext(two)` parts of the weasel `ultext(most likely)` help it detect and hunt its prey?

A.Choice: small ears; and brown fur, changes to white in `text(winter)`

Key.Rationale: Brown fur that changes to white in `text(winter)` does not help a weasel detect or hunt its prey.

B.Choice: long tail with a black tip; and brown fur, changes to white in `text(winter)`

Key.Rationale: A long tail with a black tip is not a part of a weasel that most likely helps it detect or hunt its prey. Brown fur that changes to white in `text(winter)` does not help a weasel detect or hunt its prey.

C.Choice: small ears; and claws on feet

Key.Rationale: The small ears most likely help it detect its prey. The claws on a weasel’s feet most likely help it hunt its prey.

D.Choice: long tail with a black tip; and claws on feet

Key.Rationale: A long tail with a black tip is not a part of a weasel that most likely helps it detect or hunt its prey.

Content: The students decide to leave the rocks in the rock tumbler for a `text(fourth day)`. `text(One)` student claims that the mass of the sandstone sample on `text(day 4)` can be predicted since weathering conditions remained the same throughout the investigation.
What is the `ultext(most likely)` mass of the sandstone sample on `text(day 4)` of the investigation?

Key.Rationale: The mass of the rock sample on `text(day 4)` will be less than the mass of the rock sample on `text(day 1)`.
The mass of the rock sample on `text(day 4)` will be less than the mass of the rock sample on `text(day 3)`.
Based on the pattern shown in the graph, the mass of the rock sample and on `text(day 4)` will be about `text(30 grams)` less than the mass of the rock sample on `text(day 3)`.
The mass of the rock sample on `text(day 4)` will more likely be about `text(30 grams)` less than the mass of the rock sample on `text(day 3)`.

Content: Students are studying characteristic rocks in Wisconsin. The students study `text(two)` maps comparing the types of rocks in Wisconsin and the elevation across the state. `text(One)` student observes a pattern between the rock type and elevation.
problems/WI24G4S/media/6a.jpg
Which chart shows the pattern the student observed?

Key.Rationale: The maps indicate that metamorphic rocks are mostly found at higher elevations.
The maps indicate that lower elevations have mostly sedimentary rocks and higher elevations have mostly igneous and metamorphic rocks.
The chart shows the reverse of the trend from the maps for igneous and sedimentary rocks.
The maps indicate the opposite pattern to what is shown in the chart.

Content: Engineers are exploring locations to construct a new building. They study a chart showing factors that affect rates of weathering.
problems/WI24G4S/media/7a.jpg
Next, the engineers study a chart showing characteristics of four locations in Wisconsin.
:table:problems/WI24G4S/supps/WI24G4S-T2.json
Which location `ultext(most likely)` has the `ultext(slowest)` rate of rock weathering?

Key.Rationale: Location `1` most likely has the slowest rate of rock weathering due to the relatively low `text(yearly)` precipitation, the thick soil layer, and the gentle slopes.
The higher amount of `text(yearly)` precipitation and the thin soil layer indicate that location `2` likely does not have the slowest rate of rock weathering.
The steep hills indicate that location `3` likely does not have the slowest rate of rock weathering.
The thin soil layer indicates that location `4` likely does not have the slowest rate of rock weathering.

Content: Which statement `ultext(best)` describes the feature that is most useful when an armadillo is defending itself from predators?

A.Choice: The carapace protects the sensitive areas of the armadillo from harm.

Key.Rationale: The hard carapace protects the armadillo from predators.

B.Choice: The sense of smell protects the armadillo from other armadillos.

Key.Rationale: The sense of smell protects the armadillo from predators, not from other armadillos.

C.Choice: The long sticky tongue protects the armadillo from insects.

Key.Rationale: The long sticky tongue catches insects, which are its prey; it does not protect the armadillo from predators.

D.Choice: The claws protect the armadillo from other animals.

Key.Rationale: The claws are used to dig holes in the ground for shelter and to find food.

Content: A student is describing how the armadillo detects and responds to a predator such as a coyote.
Based on the information in the passage, select `ultext(two)` processes that `ultext(most likely)` occur when an armadillo detects and responds to a predator.

Key.Rationale: The armadillo has poor eyesight, so this is not the most likely response.
The armadillo uses its sense of smell to detect other animals around it.

C.Choice: The armadillo calls to other armadillos.

Key.Rationale: No information is presented in the passage about this ability.

D.Choice: The armadillo makes a sharp, loud cry.

Key.Rationale: No information is presented in the passage about this ability.

E.Choice: The armadillo runs into its hole in the ground.

Key.Rationale: The armadillo is described as having a hole in the ground in which it lives and sleeps.

Content: Pangolins are mammals that have similar body structures to armadillos. They use these body structures in the same way as armadillos do for survival. Instead of a carapace, they have hard scales on their bodies.
problems/WI24G4S/media/10a.jpg
Based on the information about armadillos in the passage, correctly match `text(each pangolin structure)` with `ultext(one)` function.
An armadillo is identifying another armadillo it has already met.
Match each event to a box to model the order they would occur.
problems/WI24G4S/media/11a.jpg

The `text(three-banded)` armadillo has overlapping bones in its carapace that allow it to curl into a ball, tucking its face, legs, and tail inside the carapace. The picture on the left is a `text(three-banded)` armadillo and the picture on the right is a backpack made of rubber tire pieces.
problems/WI24G4S/media/12a.jpg
problems/WI24G4S/media/12b.jpg

The backpack was designed based on the armadillo’s body features. Which `ultext(two)` features of the `text(three-banded)` armadillo did engineers `ultext(most likely)` use to help develop this backpack?

A.Choice: being flexible, so it can change shape

Key.Rationale: The flexibility of the backpack allows it to change shape, like the carapace of a `text(three-banded)` armadillo.

B.Choice: being hard, so it protects items inside

Key.Rationale: The hardness of the backpack material protects the items inside, like the carapace of a `text(three-banded)` armadillo protects its internal organs.

C.Choice: being dark, so it can absorb heat

Key.Rationale: The backpack was not designed to have the same color as a `text(three-banded)` armadillo.

D.Choice: being rubber, so it is comfortable

Key.Rationale: The comfort of the rubber backpack is not analogous to a structure-function relationship in the `text(three-banded)` armadillo.

E.Choice: being made of many pieces, so it can come apart

Key.Rationale: The backpack is not designed to come apart, and this is not analogous to a structure-function relationship in the `text(three-banded)` armadillo.

Content: A student suggests that there are several ways to observe energy transfer during a collision.
Which statement describes the `ultext(best)` prediction about the results of this experiment if a student were collecting data about sound?

A.Choice: The collision in trial `1` would produce a sound that lasts for a longer time than the sound produced by the collision in trial `2`.

Key.Rationale: There is no evidence that the collision in trial `1` would produce a sound that lasted longer than the collision in trial `2`.

B.Choice: The collisions in trial `1` and trial `2` would produce sounds that cannot be heard by the human ear.

Key.Rationale: There is no evidence that the collisions would produce sounds that cannot be heard by the human ear; the student is collecting data about sound.

C.Choice: The collisions in trial `1` and trial `2` would produce identical sounds.

Key.Rationale: The collision in trial `2` would produce a slightly louder sound than, not an identical sound to, the collision in trial `1`.

D.Choice: The collision in trial `2` would produce a louder sound than the sound produced by the collision in trial `1`.

Key.Rationale: The collision in trial `2` would produce a slightly louder sound; the dime in trial `2` was pushed harder, so it transferred more energy to the other dime.

E.Choice: The collision in trial `1` would produce a louder sound than the sound produced by the collision in trial `2`.

Key.Rationale: The collision in trial `1` would be quieter than the collision in trial `2`.

Content: A student claims that the `text(dime)` that was pushed in trial `2` had more energy than the `text(dime)` that was pushed in trial `1`.
Which explanation provides the `ultext(best)` evidence from this investigation to support the claim?

A.Choice: The pushed `text(dime)` in trial `2` had more energy because it moved forward in a straighter line than the pushed `text(dime)` in trial `1`.

Key.Rationale: Moving in a straighter line does not indicate that the `text(dime)` had more energy.

B.Choice: The pushed `text(dime)` in trial `2` had more energy because it received a gentler push than the `text(dime)` in trial `1` did.

Key.Rationale: The pushed `text(dime)` in trial `2` received a stronger push than the pushed `text(dime)` in trial `1`.

C.Choice: The pushed `text(dime)` in trial `2` had more energy because it was pushed harder, and its faster motion caused the other `text(dime)` to move farther after they collided than the pushed `text(dime)` in trial `1` did.

Key.Rationale: The harder push in trial `2` means that the pushed `text(dime)` had more energy of motion that was transferred to the other `text(dime)`, causing it to move farther.

D.Choice: The pushed `text(dime)` in trial `2` had more energy because it moved more slowly than the pushed `text(dime)` in trial `1` did, so it transferred more energy to the other `text(dime)` when they collided.

Key.Rationale: The pushed `text(dime)` in trial `2` received a stronger push, so it moved faster than the pushed `text(dime)` in trial `1`.

Content: After observing the dimes collide, a student considers how energy transfer occurs in other objects. The student learns about a bicycle that is used to provide electricity. The diagram below shows the bicycle.
problems/WI24G4S/media/15a.jpg
Next, the student studies the flowchart below about how the bicycle works.
:ibox:pedals `->` wheel `->` generator `->` battery
Which option identifies an input and output in this system?

A.Choice:
input: stored energy in the battery
output: motion energy from the body

Key.Rationale: This is the reverse of the input and output for the system.

B.Choice:
input: motion energy from the body
output: stored energy in the battery

Key.Rationale: Motion energy from the body is the input into the bike system, and it is transferred to stored energy in the battery.

C.Choice:
input: stored energy in the battery
output: sunlight energy

Key.Rationale: Stored energy in the battery is the output in the system, and the bike system output is not sunlight energy.

D.Choice:
input: sunlight energy
output: motion energy from the body

Key.Rationale: Motion energy from the body is the input into the bike system, not the output; and the input is motion energy from the body, not sunlight energy.

Content: `text(Two)` students asked their school principal if the school could replace their drinking fountains with water bottle filling stations as shown in the drawing.

The principal agreed to install `text(one)` filling station and asked the students to design a way to predict whether the students at the school would use more filling stations.
Which table `ultext(best)` identifies how the students could measure the success of the filling station and an action needed for filling stations to be used throughout the school?

Key.Rationale: The measure of success is to record how much water students get from each drinking fountain and the filling station. The action needed is to allow students to carry water bottles to classrooms.
The measure of success and action needed are incorrectly identified.
The measure of success and action needed are incorrectly identified.
The measure of success is incorrectly identified.

Content: The diagram below shows how dolphins produce and receive sounds.
problems/WI24G4S/media/17a.jpg

Dolphins make sounds by blowing air through their nasal sacs. These sounds travel into the water through the melon, an organ in the forehead. Returning sound waves are received through the jaw and then sent to the inner ear. In the inner ear, sound waves are translated into nerve impulses and sent to the brain.
Match `text(each part)` of the system to a blank to correctly model how dolphins use incoming sound waves
A student studies models of waves with different pitches.
problems/WI24G4S/media/18a.jpg
Echoing waves with a lower pitch than the original sound wave suggest the object is moving away from the source. A dolphin produces the sound wave shown below.
problems/WI24G4S/media/18b.jpg
Which model best shows an echoing wave for an object moving `ultext(toward)` the dolphin?

Key.Rationale: The wave model has a lower pitch than the object is moving away from the dolphin.
An object moving toward the dolphin will have a higher pitch (frequency) than an object moving away from the dolphin.
The wave model has the same pitch as the dolphin sound wave, which means the object is not moving.
The wave model has a lower pitch than the dolphin sound wave, which means the object is moving away from the dolphin.

Content: Dolphins cannot detect fishing nets using echolocation. Sometimes dolphins get caught in these nets. A student listed `text(two)` possible solutions to improve the design of the nets.

:box:`ultext(Possible Design Solutions)`

Solution `1`: increase the size of the openings in the net so dolphins can swim out

Solution `2`: attach a device to the net that reflects echolocation sounds from dolphins
The goals for the new nets are listed below.

:ibox:`ultext(Goals for the Nets)`
`bbtext(Goal A)`: prevent dolphins from getting trapped
`bbtext(Goal B)`: help dolphins to locate fishing nets
Identify the goal(s) that `text(each solution)` meets.
The Venn diagram below compares `text(two)` applications of wave energy by humans.

:ibox:`1`. sonar (sound navigation and ranging)
`2`. radar (radio detection and ranging)
problems/WI24G4S/media/20a.jpg
A scientist wants to track the movement of songbirds as they migrate through Wisconsin.
Which explanation `bbtext(best)` describes the technology the scientist should use to track songbird migration?

A.Choice: The scientist should use radar to track songbird migration because it works in open air.

Key.Rationale: The scientist should use radar to track songbird migration because it works in open air and birds fly in the air.

B.Choice: The scientist should use sonar to track songbird migration because it works in open air.

Key.Rationale: The Venn diagram shows that sonar works underwater but not in open air.

C.Choice: The scientist should use radar to track songbird migration because it works underwater.

Key.Rationale: The Venn diagram shows that radar works in open air and not underwater.

D.Choice: The scientist should use sonar to track songbird migration because it works underwater.

Key.Rationale: The Venn diagram shows that sonar works underwater, but songbirds travel in open air and not underwater. Their migration would be better tracked by radar due to its ability to track in open air.

Content: A student pours water into a glass bottle. Next, the student gently taps the outside of the bottle with an iron rod.
problems/WI24G4S/media/21a.jpg
:ibox:`bbtext(This problem has two parts.)`
Which idea is `ultext(most likely)` being investigated by the student?

Key.Rationale: The student is investigating energy transfer from the iron rod through the bottle and water.
Although some heat energy will be transferred in the system, the student is not investigating heat conduction.
The student is not testing magnetic properties of materials.
The student is not testing reflective properties of materials.

Content: Which observations `ultext(best)` support the answer to Part A?

A.Choice:
The temperature of the water remains the same after the student taps the bottle with the iron rod.
The iron rod and the glass bottle are made of different materials.

Key.Rationale: Observations about temperature and the types of materials do not indicate that the student is investigating energy transfer through materials.

B.Choice:
A sound is produced when the student taps the bottle with the iron rod.
The temperature of the water remains the same after the student taps the bottle with the iron rod.

Key.Rationale: The observation about temperature does not indicate that the student is investigating energy transfer through materials.

C.Choice:
A sound is produced when the student taps the bottle with the iron rod.
Waves are produced in the water, showing vibration.

Key.Rationale: Observations about sound and waves indicate that the student is investigating energy transfer through materials.

D.Choice:
Waves are produced in the water, showing vibration.
The iron rod and the glass bottle are made of different materials.

Key.Rationale: The observation about the types of materials does not indicate that the student is investigating energy transfer through materials.

Content: When a dog hears a doorbell, it moves toward the door. Match `ultext(three)` of the sentences to the boxes to model how a dog responds to a ringing doorbell.
A student is looking at the diagram below, which uses symbols to represent layers of rock in an area. `text(Each type)` of rock has a unique symbol.
Limestone, a type of rock that is usually deposited when a surface is covered by an ocean, is shown by a brick-like pattern.
Granite, a rock that is commonly found in areas that have had volcanic eruptions, is shown by a pattern that looks like very short lines arranged in different directions.

Which set of labels completes the following statements to provide the `ultext(best)` description of this area?

:box:Granite is the deepest layer, which means it is the `ultext( 1 )` layer in the area. This layer was formed through the release of `ultext( 2 )` onto `text(Earth’s)` surface. If scientists want to explore for fossils, they should investigate the `ultext( 3 )` layers.

Key.Rationale: Granite is the oldest layer. The granite layer was formed through the release of lava onto `text(Earth’s)` surface. Scientists should investigate the limestone layers to explore for fossils.
Granite is the oldest layer. The granite layer was formed through the release of lava onto `text(Earth’s)` surface.
The granite layer was formed through the release of lava onto `text(Earth’s)` surface. Scientists should investigate the limestone layers to explore for fossils.
